units.content: Foundation: Levitate v0.1.0 layout renamed (namespace gf::, GF_CLIENT/GF_SERVER, GF_REGISTER_MODULE/CONFIG/SUBCOMMAND/SELFTEST, root command /gloamingforest (no aliases), log lines 'GloamingForest enabled' / 'GloamingForest world ready'), WorldDb (keys gf:<unit>:...), PackDeployer, companion net (channels <unit>.<name>), Interactions (extended with tag matchers), BlockData, Redstone, config screen, selftest framework (+ flatArea, inGloaming, captureBossEvent, snapshotVolume), e2e harness (BDS pool 5 slots, client through BeDD), CI matrix server/client + release. Generalised assemble.lua driven by merges.json (object mode = duplicate key fails, union mode for tags), layering assets/gen/{import,geo,audio}/** under manual assets/pack/**, lang merge to the 29 Bedrock locales, integer-state check, dangling gloamingforest: reference check, 'every pack file has an owner' check, block-permutation budget check. tools/upstream/fetch.ps1: read-only sparse checkout of upstream 9e40a757 into %LOCALAPPDATA%/gf-upstream (patterns exclude *.ogg and *.nbt; sha verified) shared by all worktrees; tools/ci/arr-guard.ps1 rejects any .ogg/.nbt whose hash matches the upstream tree. owners.tsv generated from id-glob rules over the pinned upstream registries: 533 blocks, 254 items, 80 entity types + spawn eggs, 22 biomes, 25 structure keys, 129 configured + 107 placed features, 634 loot tables, 525 + 15 recipes, 530 advancements, 328 sound events, 29 particles, 40 damage types, 1 effect, 4 enchantments, 154 tags, 8 data maps, 2061 en_us key prefixes, net channels, config sections and upstream config keys, 15 subcommands, 6 functions, 3 gamerules, 9 stats, 3 attributes, 4 keybinds, 9 custom gloaming/* registries, selftest prefix + dx range, e2e scenario names. All 35 contracts of the contracts table as documented headers with neutral stubs. AGENTS.md carrying every cross-unit rule, licences, the LGPL attribution header template (names the upstream source file), the unit table and the worker template.
units.description: One agent ports the Levitate foundation from GitHub (the local Levitate checkout is gone), renames it, and writes the contract headers designed backend-neutral (e.g. gf::inventory hides whether S3 yields data-driven block actors or BlockData + container entity) so spike outcomes in W0b change implementations, not APIs. It also generates owners.tsv (so F1/F2/F3 can partition outputs without waiting for another W0b unit) and the test fixture pack so W0b selftests never depend on F1's skeleton. Merged before anything else.
units.e2e: tools/e2e/server smoke (BDS loads, 'GloamingForest enabled', /gloamingforest selftest 'core.*' all PASS, world reload), client smoke via BeDD (local world, selftest), both builds + gtest in CI; arr-guard and ownership checks run green on the scaffold itself.

waves.title: Parallel contract implementations, toolchains, spikes and specification
waves.purpose: Implement every contract behind the W0a headers, build the asset toolchains (import, models, audio, templates), run the Bedrock feasibility spikes S1-S7 as each unit's first task, write the per-unit behaviour spec, and create the content skeleton so every upstream id exists before W1. Units edit disjoint directories and use only W0a headers and fixtures, so they merge in any order.

rules: R1 Ids: every id is upstream's own gloamingforest:<path> and exists from W0 (F1 skeleton). docs/spec/owners.tsv lists the owner of every id of every kind; a unit edits only files of ids it owns. Block-state names/values are frozen in docs/spec/blockstates.md; later changes may only add.

R2 Cross-unit references are strings only (block/item/entity/loot/feature/structure/sound/particle/tag ids). No W1 unit includes another W1 unit's headers; integration goes only through W0 contracts and the trigger bus.

R3 Owned paths per unit <u>: src/feature/<u>/**, src/client/<u>/** (#ifdef GF_CLIENT), src/core/<u>/** + tests/<u>/**, assets/pack/{bp,rp}/**/<u>/**, every *.d/<u>.json fragment and texts.d/<locale>/<u>.lang, assets/data/<kind>/<u>.json, assets/structures/<u>/**, assets/lang/<locale>/<u>.json, tools/{import/overrides,sounds/recipes}/<u>.json, tools/structures/<u>/**, tools/e2e/{server,client}/scenarios/<u>*.ps1, docs/units/<u>.md. assets/gen/{import,geo,audio}/<u>/** may only be regenerated by the tools (-Unit <u>), never hand-edited; a manual file with the same id overrides the generated one.

R4 Recipes: vanilla-type recipes (crafting, smelting, stonecutting, smithing) belong to the owner of the output item; custom-type recipes belong to the machine/type owner (drying U4, uncrafting U13, travellers U11, map cloning U13, casket/scepter/essence/emperors cloth U9, moonworm queen U8, no_template_smithing U7).
R5 Loot: block loot to the block owner, entity loot to the entity owner, chest loot to the unit that places the chest; shared tables (useless, just_bones, suspicious_stew, items/*) are W0 (F10).

R6 Tags live with the member: upstream tag JSON is imported W0 data; a unit adds members only through union fragments assets/tags/<registry>/<tag>.d/<u>.json. Behaviour on another unit's blocks is attached only by tag matchers (e.g. mazestone tag for the mazebreaker rule, thorns tag for the lamp of cinders).

R7 Data maps belong to their consumer (crumble_horn and transformation_powder U8, ore_map_color and magic_map_color U13, ominous_fire U22, parrot_imitations U16); compostables/furnace_fuels rows follow the item owner.

R8 One hook per engine event, owned by W0: no unit hooks GameMode, interact/use/destroy events, Mob::hurt, die, dropAllItems, block ticks, LocalPlayer movement, LevelRenderer or sky/fog functions directly; register with interactions, blockevents, combat, death, loot, entity, client.* instead.

R9 Translation keys belong to the feature owner (import partitions the 2061 en_us keys; book keys F6, death messages F10); others use tr(key, 'English fallback'). Duplicate keys in any merged fragment fail the build; the 29 Bedrock locales are generated from upstream's lang files.

R10 Sound events and particles: each event/particle has exactly one owner in owners.tsv and is played/emitted by id through fx (a missing one is silent). Owners refine audio only through tools/sounds/recipes/<u>.json; nobody opens upstream .ogg or .nbt (the shared checkout excludes them; CI arr-guard rejects matching hashes).

R11 Licensing: translated upstream code keeps the LGPL attribution header naming the upstream source file; textures/models/lang only via tools/import (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, attribution in assets/LICENSE and NOTICE); sounds, music and structure templates are original (synth toolkit, template DSL) and may follow upstream's footprint, slots, spawners, chests and loot from the spec and the LGPL template definitions.

R12 Selftests: prefix <u>.*; unit U<n> owns testPos dx 100n..100n+99, W0b unit F<k> owns 5000+100k..5000+100k+99, W2 9000+; tests depend only on W0 plus the unit itself (progression::grant, landmark::forceStart, skeleton ids, fixtures) and must pass inside the 'full' run.

R13 Config: one GF_REGISTER_CONFIG section per unit named after it; every upstream config key (TFCommonConfig ~35, TFClientConfig ~21) is mapped to exactly one section in docs/spec/config.md; shared values (boss drop chests, multiplayer adjuster, portal) live in W0 sections.

R14 Commands and functions: every /gloamingforest subcommand and datapack function has one owner in owners.tsv, spelled as upstream's literal (tp F4, center/info/conquer (+ reactivate)/genbook F6, structure_util F7, map_locator/biomepng U13, shield U9, sinister_spawner U22, travellers_gear U11); GloamingForest additions: selftest/stubs/config/reload F0, locate/place/generatebook (an alias of genbook) F6, gamerule F10, structure_util place/capture/jigsaw/templates/piece/outline/pending_probe/scale_probe F7 (docs/spec/README.md, Subcommands).
R15 Net: channels are <u>.<name>, one client handler per channel; server-to-client data goes only over the companion protocol; vanilla clients must never receive companion packets.
R16 World data keys gf:<u>:...; never keep Player* or block pointers across ticks; defer world edits from cancelled interactions to the next tick.
R17 Unknown ids at runtime are skipped with one warning per id; assemble fails on dangling gloamingforest: references in BP/data; W2 runs a registered-but-unimplemented report.
R18 W0 headers are immutable in W1. A needed extension goes into src/feature/ext/<u>/ (new files only), is called out in the PR, and is folded by A8 in W2b.

R19 Structures: procedural pieces are translated exactly; template-backed pieces use original .gft templates validated by tools/structures/build.ps1 -Check against the imported template definitions; every structure has a golden volume hash selftest reviewed once with screenshots.

R20 Bosses and trophies: boss lifecycle, bar, death chest, conquest and generic spawner come from the F8 boss kit; U5 owns all trophy/spawner/banner-pattern/miniature blocks; each boss unit registers boss::registerSpawner for its spawner block id and drops trophies through its loot table.

R21 Advancements: U14 owns all 45 advancement JSONs and their criteria; units fire their upstream triggers by string (progression::trigger) and never award advancements directly; recipe unlocks are generated into recipe JSON by F1.

R22 Both builds must pass (pwsh tools/build.ps1 -Target all -Tests) and the unit's server + client e2e scenario must pass before the PR; every e2e also runs the remote-vanilla variant when the unit has a vanilla fallback.
R23 Builds and e2e only through tools/build.ps1 and tools/e2e/*/run.ps1, which take Throttle slots; never run xmake or BDS directly outside a slot.
R24 Read upstream only from the shared local checkout (tools/upstream/fetch.ps1), not through the GitHub API (rate limits).
R25 PR title 'U<n>: <imperative summary>'; tools/ci/ownership.ps1 -Unit <u> must pass (the diff touches only owned paths plus src/feature/ext/<u>/).

deviations: Sounds and music (229 upstream files for 328 events, 9 discs) are All Rights Reserved: every event is re-synthesized (F3 baseline, owners refine, U10 composes the 9 tracks and dimension music). They cannot be identical; A7 reviews quality.

274 structure templates (.nbt) are All Rights Reserved: lich tower 182, courtyard 32, camp 35, features 21, final castle 3, quest grove 1 are re-designed in the GloamingForest template format with upstream's footprint, slots/connectors (LGPL template definitions), rooms, spawners, chests and loot; procedural structures are exact translations.

Compat not ported: JEI/REI/EMI (75 files), Jade/TOP, Curios charm rendering, CosmeticArmor, Museum Curator exhibits (66), the Tips mod (99 tips), OptifineWarningScreen, JappaPackReloadListener (Jappa textures toggle), ModUpdateURLInterceptor. Workaround: tooltips and in-game screens; tips may later become loading tips.
Structure keys quest_island, druid_grove, floating_ruins and world_tree have no implementation in upstream 4.8 and Boggard is commented out: not ported.
Locales: upstream ships 99 lang files; Bedrock supports 29 locales, so the rest (including en_ud) are dropped.

No new enchantment or effect ids for vanilla clients (Enchant::Type has 42 fixed, MobEffect 38): fire_react, chill_aura, destruction, renewal live in item user data with server-written lore and glint; frosted uses a hidden Slowness carrier. The client mod shows exact tooltips and HUD icons.

Custom dimension height (-32..256) and fixed time 13000 rely on S1; vanilla clients get per-player SetTimePacket and doDaylightCycle packets. If the native definition fails for vanilla clients, they may render below y 0 incorrectly.

Sky, aurora and weather shaders: there is no GLSL in RenderDragon, so they become CPU meshes with built-in materials (client mod). Vanilla clients get client-biome sky and fog colours and PlayerFogPacket only.

Client-authoritative movement (12 Travellers' Gear movement modifiers, yeti throw, custom knockback) is exact only with the client mod. Vanilla clients get approximations: motion packets on input edges, Slow Falling for glide, and no step-up or water walk.
Climbable custom blocks (climbable hollow logs and similar) can be climbed only with the client mod. On vanilla they are not climbable.

Custom screens (uncrafting table, advancement tree, item displays) fall back to DDUI, forms or a JSON-UI container skin on vanilla. The Java advancement frame textures are Mojang's (All Rights Reserved) and are redrawn.
Boss bars use exact RGB with the client mod and the nearest of 8 BossBarColor values on vanilla. The 15 upstream map decorations are mapped to the 30 vanilla MapDecoration types on vanilla.
Giants render with the viewer's skin (giantSkinUUIDs) only with the client mod. Vanilla clients see the default skin.

Banner patterns, trim materials and record items for vanilla clients depend on spike S6. If unknown ids crash a vanilla client, the server strips them for vanilla clients. If RecordItemComponent cannot take custom sounds, discs play through a jukebox hook and PlaySoundPacket, keeping comparator output.

Block entities depend on spike S3. If data-driven block actors are not usable, signs, chests, casket, drying racks, jars and candles use BlockData plus display entities or container entities, and vanilla clients see static geometry.
Creative tabs become Bedrock creative catalog groups (there are no top-level tabs). Durability and dose bar colours, the title splash and the Halloween visuals are client-mod only.

NeoForge config files and screen become per-unit JSON plus /gloamingforest config. The Skylight world type becomes a config option, because Bedrock has no world-preset choice for custom dimensions. Java data-pack overrides of upstream registries are baked into the packs.
The mod_exists loot condition only recognises gloamingforest and minecraft. PlateauBoss stays a placeholder, as in upstream.
Keybinds get keyboard defaults only. Touch and controller players use item-use fallbacks.
risks: S1 custom dimension for vanilla clients (height, chunk sync, map dimension id). Mitigation: F4 runs the spike first and tries both the native DimensionDefinition and the vendored MoreDimensions route; the remote-vanilla e2e gates W1.

Worldgen parity, determinism and speed on worker threads, cross-chunk trees and terraforming before noise. Mitigation: Java-parity core with gtests, F13 oracle goldens, LargeWriter, per-chunk timing budget in U2 and A1.

RenderDragon hooks (sky, world render, tint, HUD) are fragile and differ under Vibrant Visuals. Mitigation: one F12 client contract, spike S5, screenshot goldens in both modes; units never hook rendering directly.
Client-authoritative movement: rubber-banding or anti-cheat kicks for double jump, glide and yeti throw. Mitigation: U12 is isolated, has server validation, and has a vanilla fallback path.

Custom block entities (S3) are uncertain and affect chests, signs, casket, drying racks, jars, candles and spawners. Mitigation: backend-neutral inventory and families contracts, with a BlockData + entity fallback.

Content volume: 533 blocks and 80 entities mean long pack load times, Bedrock block permutation limits and client memory. Mitigation: a permutation budget check in assemble, and integer states declared as lists.

Volume and fidelity of the ARR template re-designs (274), and agents accidentally deriving from upstream .nbt. Mitigation: the sparse checkout excludes them, CI hash guard, the DSL plus validator against the LGPL template definitions, and golden screenshots.

Model converter fidelity and Molang animation limits (about 32 actor properties): multipart bosses (Hydra up to 7 heads, Naga segments, Snow Queen shields) built as linked actors can desync. Mitigation: spike S4 on the hardest models, seeded boss selftests, a multiplayer soak in A8.
W0 contract gaps found mid-W1. Mitigation: the src/feature/ext/<u>/ escape hatch, coordinator triage, A8 folding.

Hidden coupling through tags, data maps, sound events and shared loot tables. Mitigation: owners.tsv covers every kind, the ownership CI check, the dangling-reference check, and union-only tag fragments.
Machine contention: 47 GB RAM, 20 CPUs, 5 BDS and 2 client e2e slots for up to 16 agents. Mitigation: Throttle slots with a memory gate, two W1 batches, server-only iteration builds.
Symbols missing or different between the server and client header sets (MCNAPI, client-only classes). Mitigation: check headers before use, every spike compiles both targets, CI matrix.

Licensing: the CC BY-NC-SA ShareAlike and NonCommercial terms apply to the released packs, and no All Rights Reserved file may ever land in the repo. Mitigation: NOTICE/assets/LICENSE in W0a, the A7 licence audit, arr-guard.
GitHub API rate limits (hit during this review) would stall agents that read upstream online. Mitigation: the shared local checkout via tools/upstream/fetch.ps1.
Synthesized audio and music quality may feel far from upstream. Mitigation: per-event recipes owned by feature units and an A7 review loop.
Vanilla clients crashing on unknown ids (banner patterns, map decorations, entity properties, custom items in packets). Mitigation: spike S6, a per-unit remote-vanilla e2e, the A7 matrix.
buildThrottle:
Implement tools/lib/Throttle.psm1 in W0a: Enter-GfSlot -Pool build|bds|client takes a lock file %LOCALAPPDATA%/gf-throttle/<pool>/<n>.lock opened with FileShare.None, so the OS releases it if the process crashes. The holder writes its PID, worktree and unit for diagnostics, and waiters poll every 10 s. tools/build.ps1 and tools/e2e/*/run.ps1 are the only entry points (rule R23).

Build pool: 3 slots, each running xmake -j6 (18 compile jobs on 20 CPUs). A slot is granted only when at least 10 GB of physical memory is free. '-Target all' builds server then client inside one slot, and gtest runs in the slot. A separate mutex guards 'xmake require' and the shared package cache. Precompile the mc/ and ll/ headers per target type, and evaluate a shared xmake build cache so fresh worktrees do not start cold.

BDS pool: 5 slots, reusing Levitate's lv-e2e slot directory so both projects share it, with server max-threads=2. Client pool: 2 BeDD slots on the same bei-e2e.lock / hiN-e2e.lock files as Levitate.

Memory budget: about 27 GB for builds, 7 GB for BDS, 7 GB for clients and 6 GB for agents, roughly 47 GB in total. That is why builds have a memory gate.

Agent discipline: iterate with '-Target server' and the unit's selftest glob. Build the client only when client code changed. Run '-Target all -Tests' plus the unit's server, client and remote-vanilla scenarios once before opening the PR. At merge, the coordinator runs the 'full' selftest scenario and the client smoke test.

Concurrency: at most 16 agents. W0a uses 1 agent; W0b's 16 units run as one batch. W1 runs in two batches of 15. Batch 1 holds the highest-risk and most-referenced units: U1, U2, U3, U4, U5, U11, U12, U13, U14, U15, U20, U21, U24, U26, U28. Batch 2 holds the rest. W2a runs 7 audits in parallel, then A8 alone, repeated until a round is clean.

CI (GitHub Actions): server/client matrix, gtest, 'assemble -Check', import/synth/template '-Check', ownership and arr-guard. E2E runs only locally on the coordinator.
